blocks.body: # 180-row CFD matrix: two rising cases, no stationary N512

## Removing stationary N512 changes this from a week-scale job to roughly one day

The corrected matrix contains **180 rows**: capwave, Hysing rising Case 1, Hysing rising Case 2, and stationary N64-N256; native and NN cell-offset; imax 0-5. On the 128-CPU EPYC 9754 option, formal execution is provisionally **12-30 hours**, with a central estimate of **18.2 hours**. Reserve about **two calendar days** for preflight, OpenMP canaries, validation, retries, and packaging.

## Excluding stationary N512 removes most of the modeled work

Stationary falls from **5,838** central equivalent hours to about **613 hours** and now represents **84.2%** of total work instead of 98.5%. Capwave contributes 72.5 hours, rising Case 1 contributes 14.2 hours, and rising Case 2 is provisionally modeled at 28.4 hours. The Case 2 value is not a formal four-resolution measurement.

## Scope and definitions

Capwave, rising Case 1, and rising Case 2 each contain `4 resolutions x 2 methods x 6 imax = 48 rows`. Stationary contains `3 resolutions x 2 methods x 6 imax = 36 rows`, because N512 is excluded. Total: **180 rows**. There are two methods: native and NN cell-offset. `Aggregate effective speedup` combines server per-core performance, OpenMP scaling, NUMA/SMT effects, and concurrent rows.

## Methodology

Measured capwave and rising Case 1 evidence is retained. Rising Case 2 has legacy N256 evidence but no formal four-resolution imax matrix, so its workload is modeled at 1.5-2.5 times Case 1, with 2.0 times as the central value. Stationary begins with completed N64 full-horizon runs and scales only through N256 using p=3.0, 3.25, and 3.5. The central 18.2-hour estimate uses 728.1 equivalent hours and 40x aggregate effective throughput.

## The three existing generators share one cell-offset implementation, but Case 2 is not wired yet

Capwave, rising Case 1, and stationary all copy the same canonical `clsvof_nn_cell_curvature.h`, use the same overlay generator, and select weights by resolution. The header hash is `4e950902...f5dc1b`. Rising Case 2 currently exists only in the older `rising_k_provider` route; the new formal generator explicitly targets Case 1. Case 2 must be added with `-DCASE2=1`, separate output identity, and the same canonical header hash before the 180-row matrix is executable.

## Validation assessment: share with caveats

The 180-row count, shared-header paths, and canonical header hash were checked against the live repository. The time estimate remains provisional because rising Case 2 lacks a formal matrix, stationary N128/N256 are modeled, and target-host OpenMP efficiency is unmeasured. The NN statistics path also has shared writes and must be made thread-safe.

## Release rule

First add Case 2 to the formal shared-header generator and prove its manifest records the same header and resolution-specific weight hashes as Case 1. Then make NN statistics thread-safe, run `lscpu`, and benchmark N256 rows at 16, 32, 64, and 128 threads. Because stationary now stops at N256, 32x4 and 64x2 should be compared for total throughput; the measured aggregate speedup should replace the provisional 40x value before setting the finish deadline.
